name: Everline Property Group
description: Everline is a small Regina brokerage. Live MLS listings, pricing advice that shows its work, and a buying process that doesn't waste your Saturdays.

agent.name: Avery Lindholm
agent.title: Broker / Owner
agent.bio: Avery's closed more than 640 Regina deals since 2014. She started Everline because too many of her clients kept telling her the same thing: nobody had explained what was coming next.

testimonials.quote: We had two weeks to find something before possession. Avery lined up nine showings in three days and told us straight which two were worth an offer. We got one of them under asking.
testimonials.name: Sajjbur Rahman

testimonials.quote: The pricing conversation changed everything. We were about to list $30k too high. She walked us through the comparables, we listed at the right number, and we had three offers by Sunday night.
testimonials.name: Danielle Okonkwo

testimonials.quote: First-time buyers, completely lost. Every email came back the same day with a real answer instead of a sales pitch. That shouldn't be rare, but it is.
testimonials.name: Marc Thibault

faqs.q: What types of property do you handle?
faqs.a: Houses, condos, townhouses, revenue duplexes, small multi-family, and acreages inside the Regina commuter belt. We don't do commercial or farmland. If you need that, we'll point you at someone who does it properly rather than learn on your file.

faqs.q: How do I know if a property is a good investment?
faqs.a: We work through the real numbers before you write anything. Price, what the unit actually rents for around here, condo fee or maintenance reserve, tax off the SAMA assessment, a vacancy allowance, and whatever rate you're actually approved at. If the math doesn't work we'll say so. We've talked people out of more deals than we'd like to admit.

faqs.q: Do I need to hire a real estate agent to buy?
faqs.a: No. But in Saskatchewan the seller's commission usually covers the buyer's agent too, so representation typically costs you nothing directly. What you get for that is an agent working for you rather than for the listing.

faqs.q: What's the process for buying a property?
faqs.a: Pre-approval, then a written needs list, then showings. Then an offer with conditions, an inspection and financing window, condition removal, lawyer, title, keys. Most Regina purchases run 30 to 60 days from accepted offer to possession.

faqs.q: Can I tour a property before purchasing?
faqs.a: Yes. You can book any active listing straight from its page. If you're out of province we'll do a video walkthrough. Second showings before an offer are normal and we'd rather you took one.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to sell my home with Everline?
faqs.a: You get the commission schedule in writing before you sign anything, including exactly what the co-operating brokerage takes. Photography, floor plans, staging consult and the marketing budget are included. We don't bill those back.

faqs.q: How accurate is the online home valuation?
faqs.a: It's a starting range, not a number. It's built from recent comparable sales, so it can't see your renovations, your lot, or the state of your basement. Treat it as a bracket. Then let us walk the place for something you can actually rely on.

neighbourhoods.name: Harbour Landing
neighbourhoods.blurb: Regina's biggest modern build-out. Wide streets, new schools, and the shortest walk to groceries in the south end.

neighbourhoods.name: Cathedral
neighbourhoods.blurb: Character houses under old elms, and the best run of independent cafes and restaurants in Saskatchewan.

neighbourhoods.name: Lakeview
neighbourhoods.blurb: Backs onto Wascana Park. Mid-century bungalows on big lots. Tightly held, and they don't sit long.

neighbourhoods.name: The Greens on Gardiner
neighbourhoods.blurb: East-end executive houses wrapped around green space, and the easiest commute out of town.

neighbourhoods.name: White City
neighbourhoods.blurb: A quarter hour east on Highway 1. Acreage-sized lots, no city tax, best value per square foot going.

neighbourhoods.name: Downtown & Warehouse District
neighbourhoods.blurb: Warehouse lofts and concrete towers. The strongest rental yields in the city on a one-bedroom hold.
